Decide your role. Determine the ending. The Inland Empire's most immersive haunted experience. October 2026.

### Camp Coffin Creek - The Overnight Camp Experience

Camp Coffin Creek — Welcome, Campers. If You Dare.

Camp Coffin Creek is back.

Southern California's only overnight horror camp made its debut in August 2026 and sold out. Four nights. Four hundred acres. Five slashers hunting campers from 7PM until 7AM. The Inland Empire had never seen anything like it. And it is coming back.

Camp Coffin Creek is a fully immersive extreme overnight horror survival experience. You are not watching a slasher movie. You are inside one. Three professional haunted attractions, horror camp games that run through the night, an on-site special effects makeup workshop, horror movies on 25-foot outdoor screens, and a survival competition that crowns one camper the last one standing at the 6AM awards ceremony.

Every choice you make is real. Every path leads somewhere different. The outcome of the night belongs entirely to you.

2026 was just the beginning. Camp Coffin Creek returns in 2027. Join the list to be first in line when dates and tickets drop.

### Nightmare Rising Presents: Pandemic Z - What is it?

Nightmare Rising's Pandemic Z is an Extreme Haunt.

Pandemic Z is a professional immersive haunted attraction located at SC Village in Chino, California. Unlike standard Halloween walkthrough haunts, Pandemic Z is fully interactive and extreme. Guests are placed inside the experience rather than guided through it. Scare actors make direct contact, attractions involve real missions and survival scenarios, and new experiences are added every season so no two years are the same. Nightmare Rising operates select nights in October located in the Inland Empire, Southern California.

Where is Nightmare Rising Haunt located?

Nightmare Rising Haunt is located at SC Village, 8900 McCarty Rd., Chino, CA 91710. The property covers more than 400 acres in the Inland Empire, approximately 35 miles east of Los Angeles and accessible from the 60, 71, and 91 freeways.

When does Pandemic Z open for 2026?

Nightmare Rising Haunt opens October 2, 2026 and operates select nights through October 31, 2026. Operating nights include select Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays. Check nightmarerisinghaunt.com for the full 2026 date calendar and real time ticket availability.

What time does Pandemic Z open and close?

Gates open at 7pm on each operating night. The event runs late into the evening. Specific open and close times per night are listed on the event calendar at nightmarerisinghaunt.com.

What is the address?

8900 McCarty Rd., Chino, CA 91710

### Pandemic Z - Attractions

Two years have passed since Pandemic Z began.The infected outnumber the living. Cities have fallen. The highways are empty. What remains of humanity has retreated behind chain link, sheet metal, and whatever weapons could be found along the way. The fence is the only thing standing between survival and the fall of humanity. And the fence is failing.Inside Nightmare Rising Presents: Pandemic Z, six simultaneous storylines play out across 400 acres of darkness in Chino, California. Military personnel, zombie hunters, and terrified survivors must work together. Every attraction is a mission. Every mission is life or death.

Nightmare Rising is recommended for children 13 and over. If you have children that are sensitive to scares we offer "No Scare Necklaces"

Any guest 17 and under must be have waiver signed by and also accompanied by a parent

### Parking

We offer GA and VIP parking options on a first come first serve basis.

It is best to purchase your parking in advance to take advantage of our discounts and make your arrival seamless.

If your purchase in advance simply show your parking QR code to the attendant to enter, you are also welcome to pay full price using cash or card with our parking attendants.

Upon entry you will be guided where to park your vehicle.

All persons entering the park will be subject to search along with their belongings prior to entry.

# The Ultimate Guide to Haunted Attractions in Mid Missouri for Halloween 2026

Posted by Matt Smith on Wednesday, October 7, 2026 at 2:03:39 PM By Matt Smith / October 7, 2026 Comment

BOO! 👻

Halloween is here, and if you're looking for a good scare this season, Mid Missouri has you covered.

From haunted houses tucked off rural highways to spine-chilling river floats in the dark, there's no shortage of ways to get your heart racing this October.

We've rounded up the best haunted attractions across the region so you and your bravest friends can make the most of the spookiest season of the year.

The only question is, are you brave enough to walk through these doors?

Before You Go, A Few Tips

Before we dive into the list, here are a few things to keep in mind as you plan your haunted adventure:

Check dates and hours before you go.

Most haunted attractions operate on select nights in October, and some add additional weekends leading up to Halloween. Always verify current hours directly with the attraction. 

What to expect: A full haunted house experience designed to keep you on your toes from start to finish.

 

🎃 The Haunted River Float 2026

📍 22474 Restful Lane, Waynesville, MO

If you've never done a haunted river float, this might be the year you change that.

There's something uniquely terrifying about floating down a dark river in the middle of the night while things jump out at you from the banks and the water. It's an experience you can't replicate in a traditional haunted house, and the Waynesville area delivers it in a big way.

What to expect: A nighttime float experience along a river route designed to scare you around every bend. Bring a group, you'll want witnesses for whatever comes out of the dark.

Pro tip: Water can get cold at night in October in Missouri. Bring a layer and be prepared to get a little wet.

 

🎃 Rising Haunted Attraction

📍 25238 Raleigh Rd, Waynesville, MO

Another Waynesville staple, Rising Haunted Attraction brings the scares to Pulaski County with a full haunted experience that draws visitors from across the region, including military families from nearby Fort Leonard Wood.
